📡 Pezeshkian: UN speech reflected collective wisdom of Reformist, Principlist parties

📌 Tehran, IRNA — President Masoud Pezeshkian says his address to the UN General Assembly was the product of the collective wisdom of both Reformist and Principlist political parties, noting that he spoke firmly in defense of the Iranian people’s rights.

Pezeshkian made the remarks on Tuesday evening during a meeting with a group of political and social activists from Reformist parties, thanking them for the views and proposals they presented.
​
“The speech delivered at the UN General Assembly was the result of the collective wisdom of Reformist and Principlist parties,” he said. “I combined the proposals that dear colleagues had conveyed to me with my own remarks and, based on my beliefs and convictions, spoke firmly about the legitimate rights of the Iranian nation.”
​
The president also said that the fundamental basis of reformism was flexibility in itself rather than in the other side, calling for greater understanding, coordination, and unity among the country’s political camps.
​
“It is necessary, as much as possible, to increase understanding among all the political [camps] existing in the country, establish and strengthen coordination and cohesion, because divisions weaken society,” Pezeshkian said.
​
He further said his administration would make every effort to bring the Islamabad memorandum of understanding to fruition and would firmly defend the Iranian people’s rights.
​
“The point in the current circumstances is that any agreement must be based on a win-win strategy,” he said.
​
Thirteen Reformist political activists, including Mohsen Aminzadeh, Mohammad-Hossein Adeli, Azar Mansouri, Mohammad Ali Abtahi, Ahmad Masjed-Jamei, and Mohammad Javad Zarif, also praised President Pezeshkian’s UN speech and voiced support for his firm position on the Islamabad MoU.
​
They described the Islamabad MoU as “a source of pride, highly effective and decisive” in Iran’s history of developments.
​
The Islamabad MoU was signed between the US and Iran on June 17 to end the US-Israeli war of aggression against the Islamic Republic.
